ncbfb0b36c5e.s: Which of the following earlier debt-resolution mechanisms was introduced first?
ncbfb0b36c5e.x: Corporate Debt Restructuring came in 2001, followed by the 5/25 scheme (2014), Strategic Debt Restructuring (2015) and S4A (2016).

nfe855bca205.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RBI's Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets?
o: Lenders must review the borrower account within 30 days of default
Signing an Inter-Creditor Agreement is voluntary
nfe855bca205.x: The framework makes the Inter-Creditor Agreement mandatory, not voluntary; it also requires a 30-day review and resolution within 180 days.

n24569ff3e17.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for the decline in banks' NPAs?
n24569ff3e17.x: The fall in NPAs is credited to the 4R strategy, higher (not lower) provisioning, the IBC and NARCL. A match could not be built honestly from these facts, so a NOT question is used.

n8ac60d653ac.s: Under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026, the NCLT must admit or reject a CIRP plea within:
n8ac60d653ac.x: The 2026 amendment requires admission or rejection within 14 days; resolution plans must be ruled on within 30 days.

ne832b8d5ece.s: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011 to promote rural livelihoods through SHGs, is run by which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
ne832b8d5ece.x: DAY-NRLM is a Ministry of Rural Development programme launched in 2011 for rural, not urban, livelihoods.

nc5b43d0aeba.s: Andhra Pradesh, which ranks first in SHG-bank linkage, accounts for about what share of the national total?
nc5b43d0aeba.x: AP ranks 1st with about 36% of the national share; its SHG model is run by SERP, not directly by NABARD.

nindian-economy-17-3.s: AePS, which supports financial inclusion and interoperable banking, enables basic banking transactions through:
nindian-economy-17-3.x: AePS (Aadhaar Enabled Payment System) lets people do basic banking just by Aadhaar authentication.

n7eb59698902.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
n7eb59698902.x: Commercial Paper is an unsecured promissory note; call money is overnight, notice money runs 2 to 14 days and TREPS is a tri-party repo.

nindian-economy-61-13.s: Dated securities issued by State Governments are known as:
nindian-economy-61-13.x: State Government dated securities are SDLs; Treasury Bills are short-term (91, 182, 364 days) Central instruments.

nindian-economy-60-13.s: In relation to the issuer, a bondholder is a:
nindian-economy-60-13.x: A bondholder lends to the issuer and is therefore its creditor.

nindian-economy-60-17.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about bonds?
o: Market yield and bond price generally move in opposite directions
Yield is the return earned by an investor
Maturity is the date on which the principal is repaid
Coupon is the nominal value of the bond
nindian-economy-60-17.x: The coupon is the interest payment; the nominal value is the face value. Price and yield move inversely and yield is the investor's return.

new.s: A loan becomes a Non-Performing Asset when interest or principal remains overdue for more than:
new.x: An NPA is a loan whose interest or principal is overdue for more than 90 days; SMA-0/1/2 (up to 90 days) are still standard.

new.s: An NPA that has remained sub-standard for more than 12 months is classified as a:
new.x: A sub-standard asset is an NPA for up to 12 months; beyond 12 months it becomes doubtful. A loss asset is one identified but not written off.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about asset classification of bank loans?
o: SMA-2 accounts are still standard assets
A sub-standard asset is an NPA for up to 12 months
A loss asset is identified but not yet written off
SMA-0 accounts are classified as NPAs
new.x: SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 accounts (overdue up to 90 days) are still standard assets, not NPAs.

new.s: The Asset Quality Review (AQR) that exposed the evergreening of bank loans was conducted in:
new.x: The RBI's Asset Quality Review of 2015 exposed evergreening that had hidden NPAs.

new.s: The 'twin balance sheet' problem refers to:
o: Rising fiscal and current account deficits
Stressed NBFCs and stressed microfinance institutions
new.x: The twin balance sheet problem is the combination of over-leveraged corporates and capital-starved banks.

new.s: In March 2026, the Net NPA ratio of scheduled commercial banks stood at:
new.x: In March 2026 SCB Gross NPA was 1.93% and Net NPA 0.39%, a decadal low.

new.s: The Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) of a firm is calculated as:
new.x: ICR = EBIT ÷ interest payable; provisions ÷ gross NPA is the Provision Coverage Ratio.

new.s: Appeals against orders of Debt Recovery Tribunals lie with the:
new.x: DRTs set up under the RDDBFI Act 1993 are backed by 5 Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals (DRATs) for appeals.

new.s: India has 39 Debt Recovery Tribunals and how many Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals?
new.x: There are 39 DRTs, with appeals going to 5 DRATs.

new.s: Lok Adalats help settle small NPAs mainly through:
new.x: Lok Adalats, under the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, settle small NPAs by compromise.

new.s: In FY 2024, Lok Adalats accounted for about what share of bank recoveries?
new.x: Lok Adalats had a 3% share in FY24, against 17% for DRTs, 32% for SARFAESI and 48% for the IBC.

new.s: Under Section 13(8) of the SARFAESI Act, a borrower can redeem the secured asset only by paying:
new.x: Section 13(8) allows redemption only on payment of the full dues, not 25%.

new.s: Under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act, lenders holding at least what share of the dues may issue a 60-day notice?
new.x: Section 13(2) lets lenders with 60% of the dues issue a 60-day notice to the borrower.

new.s: Under the Strategic Debt Restructuring (SDR) scheme of 2015, lenders could convert debt into equity of at least:
new.x: SDR (2015) let lenders convert debt into 51% or more equity and take control of the firm.

new.s: The 5/25 scheme of 2014 provided for:
o: Splitting of debt into sustainable and unsustainable parts
Infrastructure loans amortised over 25 years and refinanced every 5 years
new.x: The 5/25 scheme let infrastructure loans run over 25 years with refinancing every 5 years; 51% equity was SDR and the debt split was S4A.

new.s: Under the Inter-Creditor Agreement of July 2018, a resolution plan binds all lenders once approved by lenders holding:
new.x: The ICA under Project Sashakt (33 banks, loans of ₹50 crore+) binds all lenders once 66% approve.

new.s: Under the IBC, which body votes on the resolution plan of a corporate debtor?
new.x: During CIRP, the Committee of Creditors votes on the resolution plan; the NCLT adjudicates.

new.s: The Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (CIIRP) under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 must be completed within:
new.x: CIIRP has a 150-day timeline and needs 51% creditors; CIRP has 330 days and PPIRP 120 days.

new.s: The IBC 2016 replaced which earlier law under which the BIFR functioned?
new.x: The IBC replaced the Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA) 1985 and the BIFR.

new.s: Under the IBC, the adjudicating authority for insolvency of individuals and partnership firms is the:
new.x: The DRT handles individuals and partnership firms, while the NCLT handles companies and LLPs.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT replaced by the National Company Law Tribunal?
new.x: The NCLT replaced the CLB, BIFR and AAIFR; it did not replace SAT.

new.s: Appeals against orders of the NCLAT lie to the:
new.x: NCLAT (Delhi and Chennai) hears appeals from the NCLT, and its orders go on appeal to the Supreme Court.

new.s: The Government guarantee on security receipts issued by NARCL is:
new.x: The Government guarantees NARCL's security receipts up to ₹30,600 crore for 5 years.

new.s: In India's bad bank structure, which entity resolves the stressed assets aggregated by NARCL?
new.x: NARCL aggregates the stressed loans; IDRCL (majority private) resolves them.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NARCL and IDRCL:
1. Public sector banks hold a majority in NARCL.
2. IDRCL is majority privately owned.
3. NARCL resolves the assets, while IDRCL aggregates them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: PSBs hold a majority in NARCL and IDRCL is majority private; statement 3 reverses the roles: NARCL aggregates, IDRCL resolves.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a trigger parameter under the RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework?
new.x: The PCA triggers are capital (CRAR/CET1), asset quality (net NPA) and leverage (Tier 1 leverage ratio).

new.s: Which of the following is a restriction that may be imposed on a bank under PCA?
o: Mandatory listing on a stock exchange
new.x: Under PCA the RBI may curb lending, branch expansion, dividends and management pay.

new.s: The RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework of 2002 was last revised in:
new.x: PCA was introduced by the RBI in 2002 and revised in November 2021.

new.s: Under the RBI Master Direction of July 2024, wilful default must be examined in NPA accounts of:
new.x: The Master Direction of 30 July 2024 requires examination of wilful default in NPAs of ₹25 lakh and above.

new.s: Under the RBI Master Direction of July 2024, the classification of a wilful defaulter must be completed within:
new.x: The 2024 Master Direction requires classification within six months, and wilful defaulters get no restructuring.

new.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) is chaired by the:
new.x: The FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not by Rangarajan.

new.s: The Y.H. Malegam Committee (2010) of the RBI dealt with the:
new.x: The Malegam Committee studied the microfinance sector after the AP crisis; digital payments was Watal and payments banks Nachiket Mor.

new.s: The 2016 committee on digital payments set up by the Ministry of Finance was chaired by:
new.x: The Ratan Watal Committee (2016, MoF) dealt with digital payments; Deepak Mohanty (2015) dealt with financial inclusion.

new.s: The RBI's National Strategy for Financial Inclusion covers the period:
new.x: The National Strategy for Financial Inclusion of the RBI covers 2019-24.

new.s: As of August 2026, the total number of PMJDY accounts is about:
new.x: PMJDY accounts stood at 59.09 crore (19 Aug 2026), up from 14.72 crore in 2015; 45.95 crore are rural/semi-urban.

new.s: Women hold about what share of PMJDY accounts?
new.x: Women hold 32.92 crore of 59.09 crore accounts, over half; about three-fourths are rural/semi-urban.

new.s: The RuPay debit card issued with a PMJDY account carries an accident insurance cover of:
new.x: The PMJDY RuPay card carries ₹2 lakh accident cover; the life cover is ₹30,000.

new.s: The PMJDY overdraft is available after how many months of satisfactory account conduct?
new.x: The overdraft of up to ₹10,000 is given after 6 months of good conduct.

new.s: The Atal Pension Yojana is administered by:
new.x: APY is administered by PFRDA, not IRDAI.

new.s: The entry age for the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) is:
new.x: PMJJBY covers ages 18-50; PMSBY covers 18-70 and APY 18-40.

new.s: Under PMSBY, the cover for partial permanent disability is:
new.x: PMSBY pays ₹2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.

new.s: The Atal Pension Yojana guarantees a monthly pension from age 60 of:
new.x: APY (ages 18-40) gives a pension of ₹1,000-5,000 a month from age 60.

new.s: The Tarun Plus category under PMMY covers loans of:
new.x: Tarun Plus (from 24 Oct 2024) covers ₹10-20 lakh for Tarun borrowers who repaid; Tarun is ₹5-10 lakh.

new.s: MUDRA Ltd, the refinancing agency under PMMY, was set up on:
new.x: MUDRA Ltd was set up on 18 March 2015, before PMMY was launched on 8 April 2015.

new.s: At the launch of PMMY in 2015, the maximum loan limit was:
new.x: The PMMY limit was ₹10 lakh at launch and is now ₹20 lakh with Tarun Plus.

new.s: The RBI created the NBFC-MFI category of NBFCs on:
new.x: NBFC-MFI was created as a new RBI category on 2 December 2011; MFIN was formed in October 2009.

new.s: MFIN (Microfinance Institutions Network) is a:
o: Self-regulatory national body of RBI-regulated MFIs
new.x: MFIN, formed in October 2009, is a self-regulatory national body of RBI-regulated MFIs.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Microfinance Ordinance, 2010:
1. It was issued on 15 October 2010.
2. It required MFIs to register with a state-appointed authority.
3. It was never replaced by an Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The ordinance of 15 October 2010 required MFIs to register with a state-appointed authority; it was replaced by an Act in December 2010.

new.s: DWCRA, an early women's group model in Andhra Pradesh, began in:
new.x: DWCRA (1982-83) was an early women's group model; NABARD's pilot came in 1992 and DAY-NRLM in 2011.

new.s: The recovery rate of SHG-bank loans in Andhra Pradesh is about:
new.x: AP ranks first in SHG-bank linkage with about 36% national share and 99.66% recovery.

new.s: NACH is used mainly for:
o: Bulk recurring payments such as salaries and dividends
new.x: NACH handles bulk recurring payments; tolls are NETC/FASTag, feature phones 123Pay and bills Bharat BillPay.

new.s: e-RUPI is best described as a:
new.x: e-RUPI is a person- and purpose-specific prepaid voucher; the domestic card network is RuPay and NPCI's UPI app is BHIM.

new.s: The National Financial Switch (NFS) was designed and launched in 2004 by:
new.x: NFS was launched in 2004 by RBI's IDRBT; NPCI took it over in 2009.

new.s: NPCI functions under which Act?
new.x: NPCI works under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 as the umbrella body for retail payments.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about RTGS and NEFT?
o: RTGS settles on a real-time gross basis
NEFT settles in half-hourly deferred net batches
new.x: RTGS has a minimum of ₹2 lakh; NEFT has no minimum.

new.s: 'Hello! UPI' is a UPI feature for:
new.x: Hello! UPI enables voice payments; UPI LITE X is offline and UPI123Pay is for feature phones.

new.s: Monthly UPI transactions first crossed 2,000 crore in:
new.x: UPI monthly transactions passed 2,000 crore for the first time in August 2025.

new.s: In FY 2025-26, UPI accounted for about what share of India's digital payment volume?
new.x: In FY 2025-26 UPI handled 24,160 crore transactions, about 85% of digital payment volume.

new.s: Through NPCI International Payments Ltd, UPI was live in how many countries in August 2026?
new.x: Through NIPL, UPI was live in 11 countries in August 2026, Bhutan (2021) being the first.

new.s: The RBI Digital Payments Index is published:
new.x: RBI-DPI (base March 2018 = 100) is published semi-annually since January 2021.

new.s: How many parameters make up the RBI Digital Payments Index?
new.x: RBI-DPI has 5 parameters: payment enablers, payment infrastructure (demand and supply side), payment performance and consumer centricity.

new.s: The RBI Financial Inclusion Index is measured on a scale of:
new.x: The FI-Index (since 2021, annual in July) is on a 0-100 scale; it stood at 67.0 in 2025.

new.s: Under the RuPay-BHIM UPI incentive scheme, which body acts as the nodal agency?
new.x: The scheme is run by DFS with NPCI as the nodal agency.

new.s: In the JAM trinity, the letter 'M' stands for:
new.x: JAM is Jan Dhan – Aadhaar – Mobile.

new.s: Which scheme forms the first layer of the JAM trinity that made Direct Benefit Transfer possible?
new.x: PMJDY (Jan Dhan) is the first layer of JAM and made paperless, presence-less DBT possible.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a part of the India Stack?
new.x: India Stack comprises Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, Account Aggregator and ONDC; RuPay is a domestic card network.

new.s: Payments banks can now accept deposits of up to:
new.x: Payments banks could take ₹1 lakh initially, raised to ₹2 lakh from 2021; they cannot lend.

new.s: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is an initiative of:
new.x: ONDC, an open interoperable digital commerce network, is a DPIIT initiative.

new.s: Account Aggregators in India are regulated by the:
new.x: Account Aggregators are RBI-regulated NBFC-AAs that enable consent-based sharing of financial data.

new.s: The retail pilot of India's e-rupee (e₹-R) began on:
new.x: The retail pilot (e₹-R) began on 1 December 2022; the wholesale pilot (e₹-W) on 1 November 2022.

new.s: Bitcoin, a peer-to-peer cryptocurrency not issued by any bank or government, was created in:
new.x: Bitcoin was created in January 2009 by Satoshi Nakamoto.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Act 2022:
1. It amended the RBI Act to provide for the Digital Rupee.
2. It made cryptocurrency legal tender in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Finance Act 2022 amended the RBI Act for the Digital Rupee; it did not make crypto legal tender but taxed gains at 30% with 1% TDS.

new.s: The world's first live retail central bank digital currency was the:
new.x: The Bahamas' Sand Dollar (2020) was the first live retail CBDC; Libra and Bitcoin are private cryptocurrencies.

new.s: Which of the following is a capital-market instrument?
new.x: Equity shares are a pure capital-market instrument; T-bills, CPs and CDs are money-market instruments.

new.s: Which of the following is a sub-market of the money market rather than the capital market?
new.x: The Call Money and Treasury Bill markets belong to the money market; the Government Bond and Stock markets to the capital market.

new.s: Which of the following is part of the unorganised money market?
new.x: Indigenous bankers, moneylenders, chit funds and hundis form the unorganised market; money market mutual funds and DFHI are organised.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the organised money market?
new.x: Moneylenders belong to the unorganised money market, which is not controlled by the RBI.

new.s: Which institutions are placed between the organised and unorganised money markets?
new.x: Co-operative credit institutions sit between the two segments.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian money market:
1. The unorganised money market is not controlled by the RBI.
2. Call money is the most unstable part of the organised money market.
3. Hundis are part of the organised money market.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The unorganised segment is outside RBI control and call money (repayable on demand) is the most unstable part; hundis are unorganised.

new.s: The Certificate of Deposit was introduced in India in:
new.x: On the Vaghul Committee's advice, CDs began in 1989 and Commercial Paper in 1990.

new.s: Certificates of Deposit issued by financial institutions have a maturity of:
new.x: Bank CDs run up to 1 year; CDs of FIs run 1 to 3 years.

new.s: Commercial Paper can be issued for a maturity of:
new.x: CP is issued for 7 days to 1 year by eligible corporates.

new.s: CBLO, introduced in January 2003, was operated by:
new.x: CBLO was introduced by the CCIL from 20 January 2003; it was later replaced by TREPS.

new.s: Commercial bills drawn by firms and discounted by banks usually have a maturity of about:
new.x: Commercial bills are trade bills, usually of about 90 days, discounted by banks.

new.s: Under RBI Retail Direct, individuals buy Government securities directly through a:
new.x: RBI Retail Direct lets individuals buy G-Secs directly through a Retail Direct Gilt account.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh plans State Development Loan borrowings in 2026-27 of about:
new.x: AP plans SDL borrowings of ₹73,383 crore in 2026-27; ₹55,518 crore was the record FPI bond inflow of June 2026.

new.s: Exchange-traded funds such as the CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 ETF trade on exchanges at prices close to their:
new.x: ETFs trade on exchanges close to their net asset value (NAV).

new.s: Investment in unlisted firms is known as:
new.x: Private equity is investment in unlisted firms; venture capital is a form of private equity.

new.s: India's corporate bond market is about what share of GDP?
new.x: Corporate bonds are about 16% of GDP in India against 79% in Korea; about 98% are privately placed.

new.s: Venture capital and angel funds fall under which SEBI category of Alternative Investment Funds?
new.x: Category I covers venture capital, angel, SME, social venture and infrastructure funds; hedge funds are Category III.

new.s: Private equity and debt funds fall under which SEBI AIF category?
new.x: Category II covers private equity and debt funds such as the Self-Reliant India Fund.

new.s: Alternative Investment Funds are defined under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations of:
new.x: AIFs are privately pooled funds defined under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.

new.s: A bond whose proceeds finance only social projects is called a:
new.x: A social bond funds only social projects; a sustainability bond funds both environmental and social projects.

new.s: A rupee-denominated bond issued overseas is called a:
new.x: A Masala bond is rupee-denominated and issued abroad, so the investor bears the currency risk.

new.s: Which of the following tends to RAISE government bond yields?
new.x: Higher policy rates, inflation and government borrowing raise yields; RBI OMO purchases and foreign inflows lower them.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about bonds:
1. A zero-coupon bond is issued at a discount and pays no periodic interest.
2. New issues of Sovereign Gold Bonds have been stopped.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Zero-coupon bonds such as T-bills are issued at a discount without periodic interest, and new SGB issues have been stopped.

new.s: An inflation-indexed bond is one whose:
o: Interest is linked to the gold price
Currency risk is borne by the investor
Principal or coupon is adjusted to inflation
new.x: Inflation-indexed bonds adjust principal or coupon to inflation; climate-only funding is a green bond.
